inputs.prompt:
Use `<image1>` as the **only outfit reference**.

Create a **photorealistic wardrobe reference sheet** that breaks down the clothing and wearable accessories from `<image1>`. Show **attire only**, **not the person**. No face, no skin, no visible body. Present the outfit on an **invisible mannequin / hollow garment display** with realistic shape and volume.

Extract and preserve from `<image1>`:

* all clothing pieces
* overall silhouette
* layering
* colors
* fabric materials and textures
* seams, stitching, buttons, zippers, buckles
* accessories
* wrinkles, weathering, dust, fading, scuffs, damage, and other visible wear

If some parts are hidden, reconstruct them logically and consistently from the visible design.

Use a **flexible multi-panel layout**. Include several full-outfit views such as **front, back, and side** where useful, plus **additional zoomed detail panels** for important parts like collar, sleeves, closures, straps, pockets, belt area, footwear, fabric texture, and unique signature features.

Style: **professional costume department wardrobe board**, clean layout, neutral studio background, soft shadows, realistic materials, sharp detail, production-ready presentation.

Important: preserve the outfit faithfully, do not redesign it, do not turn it into a character sheet, do not show a human model, and keep the result **photorealistic and detailed**.

inputs.prompt:
Create one photorealistic character reference sheet of the person from <image1>, using <image1> as the face and identity source and <image2> as the wardrobe source. The sheet is a clean grid of 10 panels separated by thin dark divider lines, all on the same seamless light-grey studio background. The left two thirds of the sheet is a grid of 8 small full-body panels in two rows of four, each panel a tall vertical rectangle. The right third of the sheet is a column of 2 large square close-up panels stacked vertically, each as tall as one row of small panels. Every panel contains exactly one figure, so the sheet contains exactly 10 figures of the same person from <image1>, with no other people, no text, no labels, no captions, no logos and no props anywhere. In every panel the person's hands are empty: they hold no weapon and no object of any kind, and any gesture such as aiming is mimed with bare or gloved empty hands.

Identity, from <image1> only: every head in every panel, including the small heads in the full-body panels, has exactly the face, face shape, gender presentation, apparent age, skin tone, natural skin texture, hairstyle, hairline, hair color and hair texture of the person in <image1>, with the same facial proportions in every view. Ignore the clothing, pose, lighting and background of <image1>. The body has a natural, fit build and height in proportion to the neck and shoulders visible in <image1>, and this build and height are identical in all ten panels. Natural hands with four fingers and a thumb, bare unless <image2> shows gloves.

Wardrobe, from <image2> only: the person from <image1> wears the complete outfit from <image2>, with every garment, layer, color, fabric, pattern, seam, strap, belt, buckle, closure, piece of footwear, headwear, jewelry item, accessory, distinctive detail and weathering mark exactly as shown, and ignore the face, hair, pose, body and background of any person in <image2>. The identical outfit appears in all ten panels, and where the sides, back or other angles of the outfit are not visible in <image2>, continue the design naturally without adding, removing or recoloring anything, so that the back views show the natural rear construction of the same garments. The outfit stretches, folds and swings naturally with each movement, and sleeve cuffs, if any, end at the wrists so the hands stay visible.

Small full-body panels: in each of the 8 panels the whole body, from head to shoes, including any extended arm or leg, fits fully inside the panel with a small margin all round, the person from <image1> is drawn at the same scale in every panel so their standing height is the same, the expression is focused and determined unless stated otherwise, and a soft contact shadow lies on the floor beneath the feet, or a faint shadow beneath the body in a jump. Each panel shows a clearly different pose from a clearly different camera position around the person, so the eight panels together show the person from the front, from both sides, from three-quarter angles and from behind. The camera position of each panel is stated below and is followed exactly. In every panel the head faces the direction the pose calls for and is not turned toward the camera unless stated. Top row, left to right. Panel 1, walking, camera at the person's side for a pure side profile: the person walks toward the right edge of the panel with the camera seeing only their left side, a natural mid-stride with the near leg stepping forward and the heel about to touch the ground, the far leg pushing off behind with the heel lifted, the arms swinging in opposition to the legs with softly bent elbows, the torso upright, and the head in profile facing the direction of travel with a calm expression. Panel 2, running, camera in front and slightly to the left of the person for a three-quarter front view: the person runs toward the camera and toward the left edge of the panel at an angle, the torso leaning forward, the near knee driving high, the far leg kicked back with the foot off the ground, both arms pumping with the elbows bent at about 90 degrees and both fists loosely closed, and the head facing the direction of travel with the face visible in three-quarter view. Panel 3, jumping, camera directly behind the person for a back view: the person jumps straight up with the back to the camera and the head facing straight away from the camera, both feet clearly off the ground with the knees bent and tucked, both arms raised above the head with open hands, the back of the hair and the rear of the outfit fully visible, and a faint shadow on the floor beneath the body. Panel 4, punching, camera at the person's side for a pure side profile: the person throws a straight punch toward the left edge of the panel with the camera seeing only their right side, the front arm fully extended toward the left edge with a closed fist, the rear fist guarding the chin, the feet wide apart in a lunge with the front knee bent and the back leg straight, the shoulders rotated into the punch, and the head in profile facing the left edge. Bottom row, left to right. Panel 5, kicking, camera behind and slightly to the right of the person for a three-quarter back view: the person performs a high roundhouse kick toward the right edge of the panel with the back and one shoulder toward the camera, the standing leg planted and straight, the kicking leg extended horizontally at hip height toward the right edge with the foot flexed, the torso leaning away, both fists raised in a guard near the chin, and the head turned toward the right edge so that only the back and side of the head and a small part of the cheek are visible. Panel 6, aiming, camera directly behind the person for a back view: the person stands with the back to the camera and the head facing straight away from the camera, both arms extended straight forward away from the camera with the empty hands clasped together in a mimed pistol grip, the feet staggered with the front knee slightly bent, the back of the hair and the rear of the outfit fully visible, and no weapon in the hands. Panel 7, crouching, camera in front and slightly to the right of the person for a three-quarter front view: the person is in a low tactical crouch with one knee on the ground and the other knee raised, the torso leaning forward toward the camera and toward the left edge of the panel, one hand touching the floor for balance, and the head turned to look ahead toward the left edge with the face visible in three-quarter view. Panel 8, standing, camera directly in front of the person for a straight frontal view: the person stands in a relaxed, confident stance facing the camera, the arms folded across the chest with both hands visible, the weight on one leg with the other knee slightly bent, the head level with the eyes looking into the camera, and a calm expression with a slight smile.

Large close-up panels, right column, each a head, neck and tops of the shoulders portrait with the face large and dominant, filling about two thirds of the panel height, the top of the hair close to the top edge of the panel, the chin about three quarters of the way down, and the collar and shoulder area of the outfit from <image2> cut off by the bottom edge, with a neutral expression and soft even light. Panel 9, top: a straight frontal view with the head upright, both ears visible symmetrically, and the eyes looking straight into the camera. Panel 10, bottom: a three-quarter view with the head turned about 40 degrees so the face points toward the right edge of the panel, the near cheek toward the camera, the ear on the left side of the head visible, the far side of the face foreshortened, and the eyes looking in the direction the head points, and the face is never turned toward the left edge in this panel. The hairstyle, hairline and facial proportions are identical in both close-ups and in all eight full-body panels.

Light every panel with bright, soft, even studio lighting and neutral white balance, with accurate skin tones and accurate outfit colors, so fabric texture stays clearly visible even on dark materials, in the style of professional photorealistic character-reference photography, all shot in the same session with the same camera and lens. Final check: exactly 10 figures of the same person from <image1>, all with the identical face, age and hair from <image1> and the identical outfit from <image2>, every panel showing a real human, eight clearly different poses, at least two panels seen from directly behind, at least two in pure side profile and at least one in three-quarter back view, so that not all figures face the camera, no weapons or props anywhere, and no text anywhere.
